subtasks.title: Select platform and tech stack

subtasks.title: Deploy testable prototype

根据 Calculator App 项目文档，该计算器的功能如下：

**已确认的核心功能（MVP范围）：**
1.  **基础算术运算**：支持加、减、乘、除（+、-、×、÷），并具备正确的小数处理和错误状态处理。（来源：Calculator App · Task brief / Subtasks）
2.  **多笔同时累计**：用户可以创建并追踪至少两个独立的“running totals”（累计总额），每个总额有独立的当前值和标签。（来源：Calculator App · Task brief / Q&A log）
3.  **计算历史记录**：提供可见且可滚动的计算历史视图，显示当前选定总额的操作记录。（来源：Calculator App · Task brief / Subtasks）
4.  **iOS原生支持**：作为iPhone原生应用运行，包含数字键盘、操作按钮和总额切换控件。（来源：Calculator App · Task brief / Confirmed decisions）

**新增/待确认的功能需求：**
*   **汇率调整**：在查看需求演示后，请求者提出业务功能应该可以调整汇率。这属于最新提出的变更请求，尚未被正式纳入已确认的任务范围或子任务中。（来源：Calculator App · Q&A log - Change requests for the requirement demo）

注：高级会计功能（分类、报表、导出）、云同步、用户认证及超出原型要求的UI打磨均明确不在本次MVP范围内。（来源：Calculator App · Task brief - Out of scope）

questions.question: Should the timer offer fixed egg-cooking presets (e.g., 4m soft, 7m medium, 10m hard) or only a custom countdown?
questions.why: Presets reduce friction for the stated 'egg timer' goal but limit reuse; custom-only is generic but requires more interaction with messy hands.

questions.question: What platform should this run on given the 'harness' project context?
questions.why: A web app needs Web Audio API for reliable alarms; a native app needs different permissions; a CLI tool is useless while cooking.
options: Web app / PWA (recommended: portable, no install)

questions.question: How should the timer handle device sleep or tab backgrounding?
questions.why: Browsers throttle background timers; if not handled, the egg will overcook while the phone is locked or you switch apps.
options: Wake Lock API + loud audio (recommended: prevents sleep)
Require screen to stay on manually

1aaa1f22944708e1bfcd8246313921a1f9a06349.title: Custom Beat & Music Builder
1aaa1f22944708e1bfcd8246313921a1f9a06349.understanding: Build a browser or desktop application for composing custom beats and instrumental music with real-time visualization and tempo control, excluding voice recording.

subtasks.title: Define Core Platform & Tech Stack
subtasks.detail: Decide between web-based (Web Audio API) or desktop (Electron/Tauri) to determine audio engine capabilities and deployment strategy.

subtasks.title: Design Instrument & Beat Engine
subtasks.detail: Specify how instruments are loaded/synthesized and how beat sequencing works (step sequencer vs. piano roll vs. loop-based).

subtasks.title: Implement Tempo & Transport Controls
subtasks.detail: Build BPM control, play/stop/loop functionality, and metronome integration as requested for pace control.

subtasks.title: Develop Audio Visualization Module
subtasks.detail: Create real-time visual feedback (waveform, spectrum, or step-highlighting) synced to playback for monitoring.

subtasks.title: Prototype MVP Workflow
subtasks.detail: Build a minimal playable version combining one instrument, basic sequencing, tempo control, and visualization to validate the core experience.

known: No voice recording required
Must support multiple instruments
User creates custom beats from scratch
Real-time visualization is mandatory
Tempo/pace control is mandatory

questions.question: Should this be a web app (browser-based) or a desktop application?
questions.why: This determines the audio engine (Web Audio API vs. native), latency performance, file system access for samples, and installation requirements.
options: Web app (recommended: zero install, easy sharing, Web Audio API sufficient for beats)
Desktop app (better performance, offline sample libraries, but heavier dev effort)

questions.question: What kind of beat-making interface do you envision?
questions.why: The UI paradigm defines the entire data model and interaction design; changing it later means rebuilding the core.
options: Step sequencer grid (recommended: classic drum machine style, intuitive for beats)
Piano roll / MIDI editor (more melodic, complex for pure beats)
Loop/sample arranger (drag-and-drop pre-made loops, less 'build from scratch')

questions.question: How should instruments be sourced?
questions.why: This affects licensing, bundle size, and whether users can expand their sound library independently.
options: Built-in synthesized sounds only (recommended: no assets to manage, instant start)
Include a curated sample pack with option to import custom WAVs
User imports all their own samples (no built-in sounds)

d577a07118201bd3c6634657d736041509aac334.understanding: Build a browser-based step sequencer with built-in synthesized sounds for beat-making and instrumental composition, featuring real-time visualization and tempo control.

questions.question: What should the real-time visualization display?
questions.why: Visualization scope determines rendering complexity and whether it serves as feedback or just decoration.
options: Waveform / oscilloscope (recommended: classic audio feedback, low CPU)
Step grid highlight synced to playback

questions.question: How many instrument tracks should the sequencer support?
questions.why: Track count defines UI layout, state management, and polyphony limits for the synth engine.
options: 4 tracks (recommended: simple layout, good for starter beats)

questions.question: Do you need to save/load projects or export audio?
questions.why: Persistence dictates whether we add IndexedDB storage, file export, or keep it session-only.
options: Session only, no saving (recommended: fastest MVP, pure playground)

baca6e5101ad962a03b670d1aed7253100062f55.understanding: Build a browser-based 4-track step sequencer with built-in synthesized sounds, waveform visualization, and tempo control; session-only with no save/export.

6da90b3ff5daa579a0def13f59ba104e086c3580.goal: Build a browser-based 4-track step sequencer with built-in synthesized sounds, real-time waveform visualization, and tempo control for creating beats without recording or saving.
in_scope: Browser-based web application using Web Audio API
4-track step sequencer grid interface (drum machine style)
Built-in synthesized sounds for all 4 tracks (no external audio assets)
Real-time waveform/oscilloscope visualization of audio output
Tempo (BPM) control for pace adjustment
Session-only usage with no save/load/export functionality
out_of_scope: Voice or microphone recording

Project save/load or persistence across sessions

Desktop/native application build

acceptance_criteria: Application runs entirely in modern browsers without installation or plugins
Users can toggle steps on/off in a 4-track grid to create beat patterns
Each track produces a distinct synthesized sound generated via Web Audio API
Waveform visualization updates in real-time synchronized with audio playback
Tempo control adjusts playback speed smoothly between reasonable BPM range (e.g., 60-200)
Playback starts/stops correctly and loops the current pattern
No data persists after page refresh or tab close

subtasks.title: Set up Web Audio API engine and synthesizer modules
subtasks.detail: Create AudioContext, implement 4 distinct synthesized drum/instrument voices (kick, snare, hihat, melodic), and ensure polyphonic playback without external assets.

subtasks.title: Build step sequencer grid UI and state management
subtasks.detail: Implement a 4x16 (or similar) interactive grid where users can toggle steps, manage pattern state in memory, and sync step advancement with audio timing.

subtasks.title: Implement tempo control and transport system
subtasks.detail: Add BPM slider/input, schedule step events using Web Audio timing for accuracy, and provide play/stop controls that loop the pattern.

subtasks.title: Integrate real-time waveform visualization
subtasks.detail: Connect AnalyserNode to audio output, render oscilloscope/waveform on canvas element, and synchronize visual updates with animation frame rate.

subtasks.title: Test cross-browser compatibility and performance
subtasks.detail: Verify functionality in Chrome/Firefox/Safari, ensure low CPU usage during playback+visualization, and confirm session-only behavior (no localStorage/indexedDB).

231149791dd3525a324d4f77f383939af444de19.title: DJ Music Production App MVP
231149791dd3525a324d4f77f383939af444de19.understanding: Build a simple DJ music production app featuring drum/melody creation, audio visualization, and tempo (pace) control based on team meeting consensus.

subtasks.title: Define Core Audio Engine & Scope
subtasks.detail: Determine if 'simple production' means a step sequencer/loop station or a full DAW-lite; select audio framework (Web Audio API vs native) to support real-time drum/melody synthesis and BPM control.

subtasks.title: Design Visualization Strategy
subtasks.detail: Specify whether visualization is reactive to live audio input or pre-rendered patterns, and choose the rendering tech (Canvas/WebGL) that syncs accurately with the pace control without latency.

subtasks.title: Implement Pace Control Logic
subtasks.detail: Define how BPM changes affect existing loops/patterns (time-stretching vs re-triggering) and establish min/max tempo bounds for the UI slider/dial.

subtasks.title: Prototype Drum & Melody Interface
subtasks.detail: Create the interaction model for adding/editing beats and melodies (grid-based, piano roll, or pad triggers) ensuring it aligns with the agreed 'simple' complexity level.

known: App must include drum beats and melody features
Audio visualization is a required feature
Pace (tempo/BPM) control functionality is mandatory
Team consensus targets a 'simple' application scope

questions.question: Does 'simple DJ music production' mean a loop-based step sequencer or a linear multi-track timeline editor?
questions.why: This dictates the entire data model, UI layout, and audio engine complexity; building the wrong one requires a complete rewrite.
options: Loop/Step Sequencer (Recommended: fits 'simple' + DJ workflow best)

questions.question: Should the visualization react to real-time generated audio or display pre-set rhythmic patterns synced to BPM?
questions.why: Real-time FFT analysis adds significant performance overhead and latency risks compared to deterministic pattern rendering, affecting tech stack choice.
options: Real-time Audio Reactive (Recommended: expected in DJ apps)

questions.question: What is the target platform and primary input method for this hackathon build?
questions.why: Web vs Native and Mouse vs Touch/MIDI determines which audio APIs are viable and how the pace/melody controls must be designed for usability.
options: Web Browser / Mouse+Keyboard (Recommended: fastest for hackathon)

231149791dd3525a324d4f77f383939af444de19.meeting_reason: The ambiguities are technical scoping decisions (sequencer type, viz method, platform) that can be resolved asynchronously by the product owner or tech lead without conflicting stakeholder interests.
